findings.what: The public fork writer follows a symlinked destination namespace and can copy a case outside the caller's requested tree.
findings.why: fork_case resolves dest before any destination containment scan. If an ancestor such as alias/ is a symlink to an external directory and alias/child does not yet exist, Path.resolve() converts it to the external path and shutil.copytree writes the full case there. Existing fork containment tests validate the source namespace only; none supplies a symlinked destination. This is a reachable path escape and violates AC7's every-public-read/write no-symlink boundary. Add a consumer test for a root or ancestor destination symlink proving no external write, then scan the unresolved destination before resolve or copy.

findings.what: A second interruption during promotion rollback leaves a valid recovery state that the next restart rejects permanently.
findings.why: _rollback restores an original artifact with backup.replace(live), but it does not update that entry's applied status or persist rollback progress until every entry is restored and the journal is finally marked rolled_back. If the process stops after one restore, restart sees status prepared/promoted plus an original/applied entry whose live file exists and backup is absent. _validate_recovery_artifacts at line 259 accepts that shape only for status applying, so it raises WorkflowError instead of continuing the idempotent rollback. The case can remain partially promoted and cannot resume, breaking AC3's durable atomic promotion/restart contract. Add deterministic public-restart coverage for interruption during rollback and make rollback progress restart-idempotent, for example by journalizing each restored entry before advancing.

findings.what: run_workflow still resolves the same snapshot twice on every loop iteration.
findings.why: After entry_phase is initialized, the first resolve_workflow result is unused and is immediately overwritten at line 198. Restrict the preliminary resolution to the first iteration, then perform one capability-filtered resolution. This is a behavior-preserving deletion that supports the task's lean-architecture objective and avoids needless computation.

findings.what: A retained test name still describes events as part of resume progress authority.
findings.why: test_resume_reads_progress_from_state_and_events_not_reports neither reads nor asserts events, while the current PRD and skill correctly state that events are observational and never resume authority. Rename it to state-not-report wording so the test suite does not preserve a stale event-resume contract.
